thread:
maria: heads-up — planning a tf apply in the 02:00 change window for cross-account IAM additions and a small transit-gw route tweak. need quick preflight and a provider/module pin.

sam: which stacks you running?

maria: infra-iam (new assume-role for partner accounts) and infra-network (tgw route change + tags). staging plan looked clean.

cheng: recommend pinning provider & modules. last rollout hit aws provider 6.x timeouts.

maria: agreed. i'll pin provider aws = 5.17.0 and vpc module = v3.2.1 for this run. sample snippet in the PR: ```terraform
provider \"aws\" {
  version = \"~> 5.17.0\"
}
module \"vpc\" {
  source = \"git::ssh://git@repo/mods/vpc.git//?ref=v3.2.1\"
}```

olivia: let's canary the tgw route — 5% traffic, wait 10m, then proceed. i'll watch metrics.

maria: good. deploybot, please queue sequence: infra-iam -> infra-network canary 5% -> wait 10m -> full.

deploybot: queued apply 1754444321 by maria. sequence set. scheduled start 2024-03-25T02:00:00Z. logs at https://deploy.internal/logs/1754444321

sam: define rollback triggers so deploybot can auto-abort if needed.

maria: rollback if within 10m of canary start: (a) gateway 5xx rate increases >2%, (b) tgw route propagation errors spike, (c) sts:AssumeRole failures for partner accounts. manual abort allowed.

cheng: also add an automatic revert for the route change if healthchecks fail. revert command in runbook: `scripts/revert-tgw-route.sh --rtb tgw-rtb-03`

devops-bot: preflight results: terraform fmt ok, tfsec 0 findings, plan size 9 resources, state lock available.

infra-bot: detected pins -> aws provider 5.17.0, vpc module v3.2.1. locking modules for run.

olivia: i've created release note stub: \"network+iam: add partner assume-role, tgw route adjusted (canary)\" https://docs.internal/release-notes/1754444321

sam: who signs off after canary passes?

maria: i'll sign off after 10m stable + olivia's OK. cheng to lead rollback if anything goes sideways.

deploybot: starting infra-iam apply at 2024-03-25T02:00:00Z (step 1/2).

sam: iam apply looks clean in logs, policies attached.

deploybot: infra-network canary apply started (5% traffic) at 2024-03-25T02:13:00Z.

olivia: monitoring: 200s stable, slight route propagation warnings but below threshold.

maria: canary stable at 9m. /approve full apply.

deploybot: executing full apply in 30s.

sam: note for ops: if any auth edgecases appear, run `scripts/regrant-cross-acct.sh` and escalate to #support.
